standard_prerequisites.name: Ampleness on an affine total space equals relative ampleness
Relative ampleness gives an immersion into projective space for finite type morphisms over affine bases
Very ampleness implies ampleness, and ampleness is stable under taking powers

proof_roadmap: Projective bundle and very ampleness (proof lines 9542-9547).
difficulty_reason: The lemma assembles six equivalent formulations of ampleness for an invertible sheaf on a finite type morphism over an affine base: ampleness on the total space, relative ampleness, very ampleness of some or of all sufficiently high powers, and the existence of an immersion into a projective space realising some or all sufficiently high powers as a twist. The proof quotes the equivalence of the first two, derives the immersion formulation from relative ampleness, notes the trivial implications, uses that projective space is a projective bundle over the base to read off very ampleness, and closes the cycle with the very-ample-to-ample result together with the stability of ampleness under powers.
